items.title: GLM-5.4 launches in Z.ai Coding Plan: first Loop Transformer from Zhipu, with vision and 1M context
items.summary: Z.ai released GLM-5.4, which loops existing GLM-5 layers for deeper reasoning and adds vision for coding, video, 3D shaders and CAD tasks. It is available through the Coding Plan and API now; weights are not out yet and Zhipu's Chinese notice reportedly gives the architecture detail (looped transformer, about 700B parameters, technical report later).

doubt.pushback: Open weights and technical report not published yet; one replier reports it looping in thought and burning tokens with no output.

reception.summary: Mostly excitement and requests for open weights, one replier reports it death-looping in thought and burning tokens, another welcomes loop transformers after Inkling 2 Mini.

items.title: inclusionAI releases LingSante-3.1 medical models under MIT: 560B-A25B flash, 124B-A5.5B air-VL and a 16.7M signal encoder
items.summary: Ant Group's inclusionAI posted open medical models: a 560B MoE with 1M context in FP8 and MXFP4, a multimodal 124B MoE for imaging and medical GUI workflows, and a small physiological-signal encoder. The lab's own evaluation claims it beats frontier closed models on HealthBench Professional; one builder is already running it on four DGX Sparks.

doubt.pushback: Benchmark comparisons are the team's own evaluation.

items.title: MemTensor and NVIDIA release MemT-1.0 memory-native models, 36B to 554B total (59B active for Pro)
items.summary: MemT models keep a persistent memory state across interactions through local and trainable hyper memory instead of re-sending history. Nano, Flash and Pro checkpoints are on ModelScope under Apache-2.0, MIT and OpenMDW-1.1; the post reports a 53.08 average across 11 memory benchmarks among parametric-memory methods.

doubt.pushback: SOTA claim is limited to evaluated parametric-memory methods and is self-reported.

items.title: WeChat Vision releases WePocketModel 1.0: 2B and 4B Apache-2.0 model that generates, embeds and picks options, with GGUF builds
items.summary: One compact vision-language backbone covers image description, retrieval embeddings and candidate selection, so on-device apps need one model instead of three. The 4B leads the paper's reported comparisons across 76 benchmarks; GGUF versions are available for local use.

doubt.pushback: Benchmark leadership is from the authors' own paper.

items.title: vLLM: KV cache offloading to NVMe matched DRAM within 1% on Kimi-K3 with 16 AMD MI355X GPUs
items.summary: vLLM skipped the DRAM tier for KV cache offloading on AMD: a 1.8 TB NVMe pool matched 1.8 TB of DRAM within 1%, and at 70 sessions 4.6 TB of NVMe delivered 5.1x the throughput of 1 TB of DRAM. Tested with SemiAnalysis AgentX traces over 48, 70 and 96 sessions; a blog post gives the setup.

items.title: Hugging Face kernels v0.19.0 makes Metal kernels a first-class citizen alongside CUDA and ROCm
items.summary: The Hugging Face kernels library now treats Metal kernels as a first-class target, so Apple-silicon kernel authors can publish and load them the same way as CUDA and ROCm ones.

items.title: SenseTime publishes sensenova-roborsi-27b: vision-language model that asks a VLA policy for motion or writes gripper-pose code
items.summary: SenseTime's 27B robot-manipulation vision-language model weights are public on Hugging Face. It either requests motion from a vision-language-action policy or writes code for gripper poses. A 9B DFlash2 speculative-decoding draft for SenseNova-Loop was published the same hour.

doubt.pushback: Aggregator post with the Hugging Face link shortened; no benchmarks given.

items.title: AlphaAnything extends pretrained RGB image generators to RGBA, with paper and model
items.summary: A paper and released model show how to adapt existing RGB generators to produce transparent (RGBA) output without training from scratch.

doubt.pushback: Short post; links not opened and no numbers seen.

items.title: TheGrill: open-source tool that tests whether a change made an LLM server faster or slower
items.summary: The author's open-source benchmarking tool works with any OpenAI-compatible server on Linux or Mac, aimed at flag-tuning claims such as one tweak out of 199 vLLM and SGLang changes that held for about 2%.

doubt.pushback: Early, small account; no results shown.

items.title: TensorFold runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on one 512GB M5 Ultra: prefill 1300 to 3400 tok/s, decode 56 to 80 tok/s
items.summary: Reported throughput for DeepSeek's own quant of V4.1 Flash on a single 512 GB M5 Ultra Mac using the TensorFold engine; the original numbers come from the TensorFold author's post.

doubt.pushback: Numbers without method or repo in the post.
